**One passage holds three faces together (Jeremiah 18).** God says, "Behold, I am shaping disaster against you and devising a plan against you" (18:11). The people answer, "We will follow our own plans, and will every one act according to the stubbornness of his evil heart" (18:12). Then they turn on the prophet: "Come, let us make plots against Jeremiah" (18:18).

findings.text: Ledger OT-H2. I held the discussion's §11 ("thought as a system", six directions of flow) as "superseded by 10.0". Two of its flows reached the narrative only in part, and two not at all: Flow 3 — thoughts acting on the self: "my thoughts answer me, because of my haste within me" (Job 20:2); "my thoughts greatly alarmed me" (Dan 7:28). Not woven.; Flow 5 — consequences returning to the one who devised: Haman's "evil plan … should return on his own head" (Est 9:25); "the fruit of their devices" (Jer 6:19, quoted in 10.2 but not for this point); "let them be caught in the schemes that they have devised" (Ps 10:2); "the plans of the diligent lead surely to abundance" (Pro 21:5). Not woven.

Discussion §6.1. Its finding that one word covers a plot, a craftsman's design and God's plans *is* in the narrative (10.3 "It designs"; 11 §4). But it appears as one example among others, and the *why* behind it is not followed. Two more items from §6.1 are missing: *dialogismos* is both inner reasoning and outward quarrel or dispute (1Ti 2:8; Php 2:14).; Picturing God by "the art and imagination of man" (Act 17:29).
